activities.anchor: Every element of formation lives in one case.
activities.caption: pair each authority with what it settled
activities.name: conFormationMatch

config.prompt: The formation cases — pair each with its holding:

pairs.right: the counter-offer that left nothing left to accept
acceptance binds on posting — the postal rule, the grandfather exception
a unilateral offer to the world, accepted by performing the conditions

config.why: The bank deposit showed intention to be bound, and using the product at the company's invitation was good consideration — one dispute, every element on display.

activities.anchor: the parties plainly meant to trade
activities.caption: run the lathe negotiation
activities.name: conLatheBranch

config.root: A seller offers a lathe at 1,000. You reply: "950 and it's mine." The seller goes quiet. A week later you announce: "I accept your 1,000."

choices.label: Yes — the 1,000 was never withdrawn
choices.feedback: Your 950 was a counter-offer — it destroyed the original offer.

choices.label: No — but a mere "will you take 950?" would have changed nothing
choices.feedback: Correct on both counts: the counter-offer kills, the request for information does not.

choices.label: Depends on whether the seller felt bound
choices.feedback: The law asks what was communicated, not what was felt.

dead.text: There was nothing left to accept — each variation restarts the exchange.

choices.label: How do I get the 1,000 back?
choices.feedback: You need a fresh offer at 1,000 — then unqualified assent.

info.text: Only unqualified assent — or a question that changes nothing — keeps an offer alive.

felt.text: Hindsight about intentions cannot revive a destroyed offer.

choices.label: Re-answer
choices.feedback: Trace what was communicated, in order.

config.why: A qualified acceptance is a counter-offer, and a counter-offer destroys the original — the distinction decides real disputes weekly.

activities.anchor: Its refinements are where students stumble
activities.caption: file each fact pattern by its doctrine
activities.name: conConsiderBuckets

config.prompt: The bargain test, refined — file each pattern:

items.label: chocolate wrappers, because the promotion asked for them
a reward promised after the act was done
sailors doing what they were already contracted to do
extra payment supported by avoiding penalty clauses for late completion
£1,000 paid of a £2,090 debt, on its own
a clear promise intended to affect legal relations, relied upon (High Trees)

config.why: Value is what the parties treat as value — the court does not police price; it only asks whether something of value moved both ways.

activities.anchor: any serious bargain can be oral
activities.caption: find the line the signature-myth would love
activities.name: conWritingSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is wrong about writing — click it:
lines: Writing is required only for specified transactions — land transfers, some guarantees, consumer credit.
The default: a serious bargain binds even when spoken.
Without writing the contract is void — nothing was ever agreed.
What changes without writing is evidence, not validity.
Consideration must exist — fairness is the vitiating factors' business, not consideration's.
config.correction: No writing does not mean no contract — the default is oral validity; writing governs proof.
config.why: The companion error is "consideration must be fair": it must exist — fairness belongs to the doctrines that police consent.

activities.anchor: rights consumers cannot contract out of
activities.caption: fill the grading machinery
activities.name: conTermsCloze

config.text: Conditions (vital terms) let the innocent party %%terminate%% and claim damages; warranties (secondary terms) attract damages only; innominate terms are graded by the effect of the breach; implied terms fill gaps — through business efficacy or the officious %%bystander%% test.
config.hint: One verb about ending the contract, one noun about a hypothetical onlooker.

activities.caption: drag the divider — void, then voidable
activities.name: conVitiatedCompare

config.prompt: Two fates of a flawed bargain — drag the divider:

before.label: Void — a nullity from birth
before.text: Contracts to commit crime; shared mistake about a fundamental fact — the ship that had already sailed.

after.label: Voidable — the innocent party chooses
after.text: Misrepresentation (the grade depending on the kind of lie), duress, undue influence — the bank and the elderly guarantor.

config.why: Frustration is the third exit — the venue burns down, war closes the trade — discharging obligations without breach, with the 1943 Act unbundling money paid and work done.

config.q: A promisor breaches cynically, purely for profit. What can the court award?
choices: Punitive damages, to teach a lesson
Expectation damages only — the bargain's value, no further
Nothing — bad faith voids the claim entirely
config.why: The measure is compensatory: in the builder example the client ends up with the promised property having paid the completion cost — no windfall. The doctrine even strikes down agreed penalties, and courts refuse to order specific performance of ordinary services.

activities.anchor: cause significant imbalance in bad faith
activities.caption: call the statutory clock
activities.name: conRejectEstimate

config.prompt: Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, the short-term right to reject faulty goods lasts how long?
config.why: Thirty — then repair or replacement, then price reduction: a tiered ladder no drafted term can strip.
config.context: The practical reading: start from the statutory floor and treat the written terms as the deviation to be justified.
